government.note: Parliamentary monarchy. Cabinets are formed by coalition negotiation after each House of Representatives election and depend on the confidence of that chamber; the monarch's role is largely ceremonial. National referendums are not part of the regular constitutional order: a consultative referendum on the European Constitution was held in 2005, and the Advisory Referendum Act (in force from 1 July 2015 until its repeal in 2018) produced the 2016 and 2018 referendums.

holders.note: Abdicated in favour of her eldest son.

offices.note: Heirs are the line of succession on 2000-01-01: Beatrix's sons Willem-Alexander, Friso and Constantijn. Friso left the Royal House on his 2004 marriage without parliamentary consent and died in 2013. Since 2013 the heir is Catharina-Amalia, Princess of Orange (nld.catharina_amalia).

system.note: List proportional representation with seats allocated nationally; the legal threshold is 1/150 of the valid votes (one full quota). seats_2000 is the result of the 6 May 1998 election; changes of group membership between May 1998 and January 2000 were not checked. The orthodox Protestant RPF (3) and GPV (2) merged into the ChristenUnie on 22 January 2000.

source.title: Wikipedia: Reformed Political League (union with the RPF formalised 22 January 2000)

system.note: Elected every four years, in May after the provincial elections, by the members of the twelve provincial councils (and, since 2019, electoral colleges for the Caribbean Netherlands, later also one for Dutch expatriates), each weighted by population. seats_2000 is the result of the 1999 Senate election as given in the 'previous' column of the 2003 election article. 'others' is the joint GPV-RPF Senate group (4 seats; the two parties' Senate groups merged in 1999), whose split between the parties was not found. Cabinets depend on the confidence of the House of Representatives, so this chamber is not treated as a confidence chamber.
